author.name: Thomas Merton
author.heading: About Thomas Merton
author.bio: Thomas Merton (1915–1968) was a Trappist monk at the Abbey of Gethsemani in Kentucky. His autobiography The Seven Storey Mountain brought him a wide readership; his later writing and correspondence addressed contemplation, racial justice, nonviolence and dialogue across religious traditions.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Merton’s chapter argues against expecting life to remain at its highest emotional intensity. His next comparison is with music, whose rhythm depends on silence as well as sound. The sentence concerns a sustainable pattern of life, rather than a rejection of joy.

schema.faqAnswer: Thomas Merton wrote a closely matching sentence in No Man Is an Island (1955), p. 127, with “and” repeated between each of the final nouns. The circulating version streamlines his wording.
schema.verdictNote: The dispute concerns exact wording, not Merton’s authorship of the thought.
